hyps.why: With node 0->2 removed, node 2 only receives signal via node 1, so a conv on edge 2->3 contributes less and may sit on a dead path.
If edge 0 is none, node 1 is zero, so placing a conv on edge 1->3 adds nothing.
When edge 2->3 is removed, node 2 never reaches the output, so editing edge 1->2 has almost no effect.
Removing the direct 0->3 edge is far more damaging when the 2->3 path is already cut, leaving few or no paths to the output.
With the deep path cut, the direct edge carries most of the computation, so making it a conv gives a larger gain.
Replacing a 3x3 conv with skip removes useful capacity, whereas replacing none or pooling with skip is neutral or helpful.
Swapping out a conv on the final edge for an identity loses capacity, unlike replacing none or avg_pool.
Filling a missing edge with a conv adds a new computation path, a bigger gain than swapping one nonzero op for another.
Cutting the input to node 1 wastes the conv on edge 1->3, so the drop is larger when that conv exists.
Replacing a 3x3 conv with parameter-free pooling loses capacity, while replacing none or skip with pooling costs little.
